tutor.sk: Dobrý deň! Vitajte. Čo vám prinesiem?
tutor.en: Hello! Welcome. What shall I bring you?

options.sk: Dobrý deň. Ja chcieť kávu, prosím.
options.why: Slovak needs the conjugated verb here: 'chcem' (I want), not the infinitive 'chcieť'.
Coffee is the object, so it takes the accusative: 'kávu', not the instrumental 'kávou'.

tutor.sk: Hneď bude. Chcete stôl pri okne?
tutor.en: It will be right there. Would you like a table by the window?

options.why: 'Pri' takes the locative: 'pri okne'; 'oknu' is the dative.
'Pri okne' means by the window; 'na okno' would mean onto the window.

tutor.sk: Hneď vám ho prinesiem. Máme aj čokoládový koláč.
tutor.en: I'll bring it right away. We also have chocolate cake.

options.sk: Výborne, dám si aj koláč. Ďakujem.
Výborne, dám si aj koláču. Ďakujem.
options.why: 'Koláču' is the genitive; the direct object takes the accusative: 'koláč'.

options.sk: Výborne, dám si aj kávu. Ďakujem.
options.why: 'Kávu' is the coffee you already ordered — this offer is the cake: 'koláč'.
After 's' meaning with, the instrumental follows: 's mliekom'; 'mlieku' is a dative/locative form.

tutor.sk: Dobre. Niečo ešte? Máme aj dobrý chlieb.
tutor.en: Good. Anything else? We also have good bread.

options.why: 'Ďakujem' is I thank you; 'ďakujeme' is we thank you — one person ordering says 'ďakujem'.
'Ďakujem za' takes the accusative: 'za chlieb'; 'chliebom' is instrumental.

tutor.sk: Tak to je 4 eurá a 20 centov.

options.why: Paying BY card is instrumental: 'kartou'; 'karte' is the locative/dative.
The first person needs the conjugated 'zaplatím' (I will pay), not the infinitive 'zaplatiť'.
When leaving you say 'dovidenia' (goodbye); 'dobrý deň' is the hello.
Goodbye is one word in Slovak: 'dovidenia'.
